title: Salcedo Avocado: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Salcedo Avocado: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Salcedo avocado is an avocado variety from Alejandro Tabayocyoc. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Salcedo is a registered avocado variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1999 as NSIC 1999 Av 04. Alejandro Tabayocyoc bred it. Its record notes a yield of 300 to 400 fruits.

items: **Yield:** a recorded yield of 300 to 400 fruits.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Salcedo was about 15 years old when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 300 to 400 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in June August. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit avocado fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A fruit of Salcedo weighs about 667.95 grams, and its shape is ovoid. The flesh is yellow and smooth. The edible part is 77.1 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is June August, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Salcedo avocado

Grafted avocado bears sooner and true to type. Pick a selection by fruit size and flesh, and plant two kinds that flower at different times of day for better fruit set. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Salcedo?
